---
title: "Warping"
description: "gdalxarray.warp() builds a warped-VRT recipe; xarray opens it lazily."
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
from _common import *
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

`gdalxarray.warp()` wraps `gdal.Warp(..., format="VRT")` and returns
the VRT as a string. Nothing is resampled until values are read, and
then only for the cells asked for. The recipe is a few kilobytes
whatever the size of the source.

## A polar grid to longitude and latitude

The fixture is a 500 x 400 float32 COG in Antarctic Polar Stereographic
(EPSG:3031), with nodata:

```{python}
polar = fixture("cog/polar-f32-zstd-bigtiff.tif")
src = xr.open_dataset(polar, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
src["band_data"].shape, src.xindexes["crs"].crs.to_epsg()
```

```{python}
recipe = gdalxarray.warp(polar, crs="EPSG:4326", bbox=(-180, -90, 180, -50),
                         resolution=(0.5, 0.25), resampling="bilinear")
print(f"{len(recipe)} characters of VRT")
print("\n".join(recipe.splitlines()[:6]))
```

The recipe opens like any other source, in classic mode:

```{python}
ll = xr.open_dataset(recipe, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
ll["band_data"]
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "The polar fixture as stored (left) and warped to longitude/latitude south of 50S (right)."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1.6]))
kw = dict(cmap="viridis", vmin=float(src.band_data.min()), vmax=float(src.band_data.max()))
src["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=axs[0], add_colorbar=False, **kw)
axs[0].set_aspect("equal"); axs[0].set_title("EPSG:3031, as stored")
ll["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=axs[1], **kw)
axs[1].set_title("EPSG:4326, warped on read")
plt.show()
```

## Any target the warper can express

Target CRS, extent and size are all recipe parameters. The same global
fixture in three projections, the last centred on Hobart:

```{python}
world = fixture("cog/world-int16-deflate.tif")
targets = {
    "Antarctic polar stereographic": dict(crs="EPSG:3031", bbox=(-4e6, -4e6, 4e6, 4e6), shape=(300, 300)),
    "Equal Earth": dict(crs="+proj=eqearth", bbox=(-17.3e6, -8.4e6, 17.3e6, 8.4e6), shape=(500, 243)),
    "Orthographic over Hobart": dict(crs="+proj=ortho +lat_0=-42.9 +lon_0=147.3",
                                     bbox=(-6.4e6, -6.4e6, 6.4e6, 6.4e6), shape=(300, 300)),
}
warped = {k: xr.open_dataset(gdalxarray.warp(world, resampling="bilinear", **t),
                             engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)["band_data"].isel(band=0)
          for k, t in targets.items()}
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "One int16 COG, three warped VRT recipes. Cells outside the projection's domain are nodata."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1.8, 1]))
for ax, (name, da) in zip(axs, warped.items()):
    ax.imshow(np.ma.masked_invalid(da.values), cmap="cividis")
    ax.set_title(name); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()
```

Extra keywords go straight to `gdal.WarpOptions`, so cutlines,
transformer options, geolocation arrays, working type and so on are
available. [Curvilinear grids](curvilinear.qmd) uses `geoloc=True`.

## Checked against GDAL

wxylib/fixtures carries what `gdal.Warp` wrote for a set of target
grids over these COGs (into in-memory datasets, single-threaded, error
threshold 0.125). For each case this page compares:

- **gdalxarray**: `gdalxarray.warp()` opened with xarray;
- **GDAL VRT**: the same warped VRT read by GDAL itself
  (`gdal.Warp(format="VRT")` then `ReadAsArray`);
- **GDAL direct**: `gdal.Warp` into memory with the fixture's settings,
  using the GDAL this page was built with;
- **pinned**: the fixture's recorded result, from the GDAL version in
  its manifest.

gdalxarray must agree with the GDAL VRT on every cell: that is the
claim this package makes, that it adds nothing to what GDAL reads. The
other two columns are reported, not required. A warped VRT computes
each block on its own, so where the approximate transformer struggles
(near a pole, say) it can differ from a single direct warp; and GDAL's
resampling kernels change between releases.

```{python}
from osgeo import osr

man = fixture_json("warp/manifest.json")


def warp_now(c, method):
    s = gdal.Open(fixture(c["source"]))
    nd = s.GetRasterBand(1).GetNoDataValue()
    srs = osr.SpatialReference(); srs.SetFromUserInput(c["crs"])
    dst = gdal.GetDriverByName("MEM").Create("", c["width"], c["height"], s.RasterCount,
                                             s.GetRasterBand(1).DataType)
    dst.SetGeoTransform(c["geotransform"]); dst.SetProjection(srs.ExportToWkt())
    for b in range(1, s.RasterCount + 1):
        band = dst.GetRasterBand(b)
        if nd is not None:
            band.SetNoDataValue(nd)
        band.Fill(nd if nd is not None else 0)
        gdal.Warp(dst, s, options=gdal.WarpOptions(
            srcBands=[b], dstBands=[b], resampleAlg=method, srcNodata=nd, dstNodata=nd,
            errorThreshold=0.125, warpMemoryLimit=c["warp_memory_mb"], multithread=False,
            overviewLevel="AUTO" if c["overview"] != "none" else "NONE",
            warpOptions=["INIT_DEST=NO_DATA"] if nd is not None else []))
    return dst.ReadAsArray().reshape(s.RasterCount, c["height"], c["width"])


def same(a, b):
    return float(np.mean((a == b) | (np.isnan(a) & np.isnan(b)))) if a.dtype.kind == "f" \
        else float(np.mean(a == b))


rows = []
for c in man["cases"]:
    if c["warp_memory_mb"] < 64 or c.get("wrap_globe"):
        continue   # chunked-warp and wrap cases: see the wxylib explainers
    gt, W, H = c["geotransform"], c["width"], c["height"]
    bbox = (gt[0], gt[3] + gt[5] * H, gt[0] + gt[1] * W, gt[3])
    for r in c["results"]:
        kw = dict(crs=c["crs"], bbox=bbox, shape=(W, H), resampling=r["resampling"],
                  errorThreshold=0.125)
        if c["overview"] == "none":
            kw["overviewLevel"] = "NONE"
        vrt = gdalxarray.warp(fixture(c["source"]), **kw)
        gx = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False,
                             mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values
        vrt_gdal = gdal.Open(vrt).ReadAsArray().reshape(gx.shape)
        direct = warp_now(c, r["resampling"])
        pinned = fixture_array("warp/" + r["file"], c["dtype"]).reshape(gx.shape)
        rows.append({"case": c["name"], "resampling": r["resampling"],
                     "gdalxarray = GDAL VRT": same(gx, vrt_gdal),
                     "GDAL VRT = GDAL direct": same(vrt_gdal, direct),
                     "GDAL direct = pinned": same(direct, pinned)})

tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)
tab.style.format("{:.2%}", subset=tab.columns[2:]).hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
bad = tab[tab["gdalxarray = GDAL VRT"] < 1]
print(f"Pinned oracle from GDAL {man['gdal']}; this page built with GDAL {gdal.__version__}. "
      f"gdalxarray matches GDAL's own read of the VRT in {len(tab) - len(bad)} of {len(tab)} cases; "
      f"{(tab['GDAL direct = pinned'] == 1).sum()} of {len(tab)} direct warps match the pinned oracle exactly.")
print()
assert bad.empty, bad
```
